safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated includes sore throat and blocked ears but does not document runny nose.

This mainly represents loss of clinical nuance and may prompt unnecessary follow-up questions.

safety_verdicts.content: A delayed prescription for Amoxicillin was provided, to be started in 24-48 hours if symptoms do not improve.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated mentions a prescription and a 24–40 hour timeframe but does not specify amoxicillin nor the delayed/conditional instruction (start in 24–48h if not improving).
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting the antibiotic name and, more importantly, the delayed/conditional start instructions can result in inappropriate immediate antibiotic use or, conversely, failure to start when intended—both of which can adversely affect outcomes and stewardship. This is a medication/plan clarity error with meaningful potential downstream impact.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient to have a review in one week if not better.

This primarily increases the chance of delayed follow-up and additional care utilization.

safety_verdicts.content: Diabetes mellitus (patient states “type two” then “type one”; type unclear)
